name: vlayer

hlido_opinion.headline: Zero-knowledge infrastructure that lets Ethereum smart contracts verify real-world data — powerful primitives (Web/Email Proofs, Time Travel, Teleport), but reviewed here through docs the site itself flags as outdated.
hlido_opinion.body: vlayer is developer infrastructure for the Web3 stack: it lets Ethereum smart contracts extract, verify and integrate real-world data using zero-knowledge proofs and multi-party computation, so a contract can act on a fact without the underlying private data ever being exposed. The four primitives are genuinely interesting and clearly scoped — Web Proofs (verify data from APIs and websites on-chain), Email Proofs (bring email content on-chain, e.g. to reset an account-abstraction wallet), Time Travel (use historical on-chain balances for airdrops, voting or entitlements) and Teleport (execute a contract across EVM-compatible chains). The use-cases are concrete rather than hand-wavy: proof of asset custody, proof-of-holdings as cross-chain loan collateral, verifiable social-media engagement for brand partnerships. It is distributed as a developer toolkit — install the CLI, scaffold a project, and drive it from Vanilla JS/TS or React. What holds the score down is not the technology but the surface we could review: the reviewed page is the `book.vlayer.xyz` handbook, which opens with its own banner saying the docs are outdated and pointing to a newer site, so the first thing a developer (or an agent) meets is a self-declared stale reference. There is no pricing, no maturity or production-readiness signal, and the proof primitives require a blockchain environment to exercise, so this is a review of documentation, not of behaviour. For teams already building on Ethereum who need verifiable off-chain data, the primitives are worth a serious look — but the public entry point needs to stop sending readers to a page it admits is out of date.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) because vlayer offers real, well-differentiated ZK/MPC primitives with concrete on-chain use-cases and a documented JS/TS + React developer path. Held in the low band because the reviewed surface is a handbook the site itself flags as outdated, no pricing or production-maturity evidence is public, and the proofs can only be exercised inside a blockchain environment — so this is a documentation review, not a behavioural one. It rises with a current, non-deprecated docs entry point and public evidence of production usage.
what_it_does_well: Clearly-scoped ZK/MPC primitives — Web Proofs, Email Proofs, Time Travel and Teleport — each mapped to concrete real-world applications
Solves a genuine problem: acting on verified facts on-chain without exposing the underlying private data
Documented developer path from Vanilla JS/TS and React, with installation and first-project steps
Cross-chain execution (Teleport) and historical on-chain reads (Time Travel) are differentiated capabilities, not table stakes
what_it_fails_at: The reviewed docs page (book.vlayer.xyz) carries its own banner saying it is outdated and points elsewhere — a poor public entry point
No pricing or access model visible on the reviewed surface
No production-maturity, security-audit or adoption evidence on the captured surface
The primitives require a blockchain environment to exercise — nothing is behaviourally testable from the public page
No MCP server or agent-native interface surfaced
best_for: Ethereum / EVM developers who need to bring verified off-chain or historical on-chain data into smart contracts
Teams building account-abstraction, airdrop, entitlement or cross-chain-collateral flows that depend on provable facts
Web3 builders comfortable evaluating ZK/MPC tooling from source and current docs
not_recommended_for: Non-blockchain teams — the entire value proposition assumes smart-contract deployment
Buyers who need published pricing or a production-readiness signal before evaluating
Agent-driven workflows expecting an MCP server or hosted API rather than an on-chain SDK
red_flags: The primary reviewed documentation page declares itself outdated and redirects readers to a different site

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: vlayer is a developer SDK/CLI for Ethereum smart-contract development (Vanilla JS/TS and React), not a hosted agent surface. An agent could consume it only as a code library within a blockchain project; there is no MCP server or hosted API on the reviewed surface, and the proofs require a chain environment to run.
